bandReport.notes: COMPLETE. Band is Q66-Q79, all 14 self-contained. NO Directions blocks, NO figures, NO data tables anywhere on p12-p15 - every question stands alone. SEAMS: p11 (owned by b3) ends with Q65 complete at the foot of its right column, so Q66 opens my band cleanly; p16 (owned by b5) opens with Q80 complete, and Q79's option (d) is the last printed line of my p15, so nothing straddles either seam. STRUCTURE: p12-p13 and the top of p14 are a run of five 'A question is given followed by two statements I and II' data-sufficiency items (Q66-Q70), continuing the run that started before my band on p11 (Q64-Q65 there, and b3 reports Q61 in the same style); these carry their own Question/Statement-I/Statement-II inline and are NOT a shared-stimulus set, so each is transcribed whole and standalone. Q71's stem sits at the foot of p14's LEFT column with its four options at the head of the RIGHT column - ordinary two-column flow, not a seam. Source PDF pages 12-15 have NO text layer (0 chars), so every reading is visual; all numerals, exponents and signs were re-checked from the PDF at 6-9x.

questions.stem:
A question is given followed by two statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements and mark the correct option.

Question : The ratio of \(P\)'s salary to \(Q\)'s salary is \(6 : 5\). How much is \(P\)'s expenditure ?

Statement-I : The ratio of \(P\)'s saving to \(Q\)'s saving is \(3 : 2\)

Statement-II : The ratio of \(P\)'s expenditure to \(Q\)'s expenditure is \(1 : 1\)

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements ?

options.label: A
options.text: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other Statement alone

options.label: B
options.text: The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone

options.label: C
options.text: The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone

options.label: D
options.text: The Question cannot be answered even by using both the Statements together
